title: Level 5 (World Class) - B-9
notes:
West leads the ♥K against 6♠. West's heart lead offers a ruff and discard for South. A discard from dummy will be useless. South clearly should keep all of the clubs in the closed hand. If the defense can hold up the ♣A twice, South may need need all 3 of his diamonds.

South has plenty of trumps to spare. The first trick should be ruffed in both hands. South should draw trump and lead the ♣K forcing the defense to duck.

South overtakes the ♣J with the ♣Q (or leads the ♣2 to a low club in dummy) and the defense must duck again. The club suit is dead, but South still has a chance if East has the ♣A along with a doubleton diamond including either the ♦K or ♦Q and either the ♦9 or ♦8.

A diamond is played to the ♦8 (the ♦K would not help), ♦10, and ♦Q (ducking would not help). West must return a diamond and a low card is played from dummy. East's ♦K is taken by the ♦A. The diamonds can be played for 2 more tricks by finessing against the ♦9. The fourth round of diamonds will provide a discard for South's club loser.
